body: NVIDIA's **data-center revenue was $339M in FY16, $1.93B in FY18 and $10.6B in FY22**, all years before ChatGPT ([StockAnalysis](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/nvda/metrics/data-center-revenue/); [NVIDIA investor presentation, Oct 2022](https://s201.q4cdn.com/141608511/files/doc_presentations/2022/NVIDIA-Investor-Presentation-Oct-2022-(1).pdf)). The signal was a small segment compounding inside a company the market mostly saw as a gaming and crypto business. Holders had to sit through **two drawdowns of more than 50%, in 2018 and 2022** ([Yahoo Finance/Motley Fool](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/nvidia-down-27-peak-history-100700214.html)). Both came from the cyclical gaming and crypto segment, not from the data-center thesis. After 2023 the stock's gains came "primarily [from] earnings growth rather than renewed multiple expansion" ([Mavengity](https://mavengity.com/articles/finance/nvidia-valuation-duration-not-existence/)). **Forward P/E fell from about 40 in mid-2025 to about 15–17x by October–November 2026** ([shattered.io](https://shattered.io/nvidia-17x-forward-earnings-cheap-multiple-half-story-2026/); [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/nvidia-nvda-more-doubled-revenue-132539113.html)). The bear case also deserves its due. If expected EPS growth of 70% turns out to be 40%, "17x was never 17x" ([shattered.io](https://shattered.io/nvidia-17x-forward-earnings-cheap-multiple-half-story-2026/)). Several commonly told details are **unverified in this research**: the CUDA launch in 2006–07, AlexNet being trained on GTX 580s in 2012, the May 2023 guidance shock, and ARK selling early.

Sundar's fame rests on selling Nifty, Bank Nifty and stock options to collect time decay. His audience is about 1.2 million YouTube subscribers, and he sells paid workshops ([ISFM](https://isfm.co.in/p-r-sundar-net-worth/)). His trading returns are entirely self-reported. He calls 25–30% a year "very good" ([X](https://x.com/PRSundar64/status/1696158361501261954)), and his own tweet shows the tail risk of the strategy: "Lost 15 lakhs as I sold Call options yesterday" ([X](https://twitter.com/PRSundar64/status/1215213725033984000)).

The verifiable money is in SEBI's **settlement order of 25 May 2023**, not 2024. SEBI found that his company, Mansun Consultancy, sold "daily calls on Telegram" through his blog without investment-adviser registration and collected **₹4,59,95,763** in fees. Sundar, his wife and the company settled without admitting or denying the findings. They paid **₹6,07,69,863 in disgorgement** (fees plus 12% interest) and ₹46.8 lakh in settlement amounts, and accepted a one-year bar from dealing in securities ([SEBI order](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/attachdocs/may-2023/1685095933750.pdf)). Media reports of a "₹6.5 crore penalty" round these figures together. SEBI has since gone after the same pattern of "education" that is really advice. It ordered "Baap of Chart" to refund ₹17 crore ([BQ Prime](https://www.bqprime.com/law-and-policy/sebi-bars-baap-of-chart-finfluencer-orders-rs-17-crore-refund)), and in December 2025 impounded more than ₹546 crore from Avadhut Sathe's trading academy ([JusCorpus](https://www.juscorpus.com/educators-or-unlicensed-advisers/)). For a famous market personality, the dependable income is fees from followers. Trading profits are optional and unaudited.

body:
**CAN SLIM (William O'Neil, *How to Make Money in Stocks*)**
- C = Current quarterly EPS up at least 25% year over year (O'Neil preferred 40%+); accelerating growth is a positive. — [AAII: O'Neil's CAN SLIM approach](https://www.aaii.com/journal/article/william-oneil-can-slim-approach-to-selecting-growth-stocks) [F]; [Wikipedia: CAN SLIM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CAN_SLIM) [F]
- A = Annual EPS growth of 25%+ in each of the last 3 years (some sources say 3-5 years); ROE of at least 17% (O'Neil's studies of the biggest winners). Some screens add sales growth of 25%+ as confirmation. — [AAII](https://www.aaii.com/journal/article/how-to-use-the-can-slim-approach-to-screen-for-growth-stocks) [F]; [Liberated Stock Trader: What is CANSLIM](https://www.liberatedstocktrader.com/what-is-canslim/) [F]
- N = Something New: new product/service, new management, or new industry conditions, and the stock emerging from a proper base to new price highs. — [Wikipedia: CAN SLIM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CAN_SLIM) [K]
- S = Supply and demand: shares outstanding/float, and price advances on volume well above average (accumulation). — [Wikipedia: CAN SLIM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CAN_SLIM) [K]
- L = Leader or laggard: buy leaders in leading industry groups; IBD Relative Strength Rating of 80+ (O'Neil). — [AAII](https://www.aaii.com/journal/article/william-oneil-can-slim-approach-to-selecting-growth-stocks) [K]
- I = Institutional sponsorship: increasing number of quality institutional owners in recent quarters. — [Wikipedia: CAN SLIM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CAN_SLIM) [K]
- M = Market direction: roughly 3 of 4 stocks follow the general market, so buy only in a confirmed uptrend (follow-through day), and cut exposure as distribution days pile up. — [Wikipedia: CAN SLIM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CAN_SLIM) [K]
- Sell rule: cut every loss at 7-8% below purchase price, no exceptions; O'Neil's typical profit-taking zone is 20-25% gains (with an exception to hold for 8 weeks a stock that gains 20%+ within 3 weeks of breakout). — [Liberated Stock Trader](https://www.liberatedstocktrader.com/what-is-canslim/) [F] for the 7-8% stop; 20-25%/8-week rule is [K] from the book.
- Cup-with-handle: online sources disagree on parameters. One guide lists 7-65 weeks duration and 15-35% depth; O'Neil's book describes bases of at least 7 weeks and cups typically 12-33% deep (up to ~40-50% in bear markets), handle drifting down in the upper half of the base, ideally on light volume, buy point = handle high + $0.10, breakout volume 40-50%+ above average. — [AAII screening guide](https://www.aaii.com/journal/article/how-to-use-the-can-slim-approach-to-screen-for-growth-stocks) [F] (conflict noted); book parameters [K].
- Flat base: per O'Neil, a ~5+ week sideways base correcting no more than ~10-15%, often forming after a breakout from a cup. [K] — [Wikipedia: CAN SLIM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CAN_SLIM)
- AAII's long-running CAN SLIM screen has been one of its better-performing screens historically (AAII publishes the track record), but this is a screen backtest, not an audited live record. — [AAII](https://www.aaii.com/journal/article/how-to-use-the-can-slim-approach-to-screen-for-growth-stocks) [K]

`case_study:india-bull-2003-08` | confidence: **verified** | tags: india, cyclical, sector-realty, sector-infra, rerating, base-rate

Sensex ~2,900 (April 2003) to 21,206.77 (10 Jan 2008), about 7x in under five years. Drivers: GDP growth 8-9%, ~30% credit growth, a corporate capex boom, a global commodity super-cycle and record FII inflows. Leaders: real estate (DLF IPO July 2007, then India's largest; Unitech), infrastructure developers and power (GMR, GVK, Lanco, Reliance Power), capital goods (BHEL, L&T, Suzlon), metals. Laggards: IT (after 2000), FMCG and pharma - defensives looked 'boring'. Valuation at peak: Sensex trailing P/E ~27-28x; market cap/GDP widely cited near 150% (one Business Standard figure is dated 'Dec 2017', likely meaning 2007). Top signals visible at the time: Reliance Power's Jan 2008 IPO (~Rs 11,560 crore, oversubscribed ~70x, listed below its issue price on 11 Feb 2008 - detail from memory), Sensex 10k to 20k in ~2 years, mid/small caps outrunning large caps, infra companies valued on land banks and order books rather than cash flows, rising leverage. What followed: a ~61% Sensex crash; the Indian capital goods index needed until ~2021 to regain its 2007-08 peak; Nifty Realty remains far below its 2008 high (unverified current level). Lesson: a capex-and-credit boom produces the biggest losses in the sectors that led it; land-bank and order-book valuations are reflexive.

body:
**Hidden trap: Gitanjali Gems' revenue and 'standard' loans** (`case_study:hidden-trap-gitanjali-receivables`, verified). THE GOOD NUMBER: Gitanjali Gems reported large revenues and profits, ran well-known jewellery brands, and its bank loans were 'standard' with regular debt servicing until Dec 2017; over 30 lenders (SBI, StanChart, BoI, BoB...) were exposed per the FY17 annual report. WHY IT LIED: a large share of its business was with its own group: group-company receivables were reported at ~33% of the company's total receivables, so 'sales' partly moved money within the promoter's network. Import trade was financed by letters of undertaking from PNB with credit of ~360 days against RBI's 90-day norm for precious-stone imports; PNB later found 151 fraudulent LoUs and no proof the trades were bona fide. Feb 2018: PNB declared the fraud (Nirav Modi/Mehul Choksi); Gitanjali fell ~61% in seven days. TELLS THAT WERE PUBLIC OR SEMI-PUBLIC: SMA-2 classification in 2014 after >60-day payment delays; a March 2017 auditor warning of default to LIC; a sharp fall in promoter Mehul Choksi's shareholding; sector receivables at ~5 months of sales (CARE). TEST: related-party share of receivables and sales; receivable days vs domestic peers; whether credit periods exceed regulatory norms; promoter stake trend. LESSON: receivables owed by your own group are not assets; pre-2018 debtor-days data was not found this session [gap].

**Hidden trap: Cox & Kings' 250-year brand and reported profits** (`case_study:hidden-trap-cox-and-kings-brand`, single-source). THE GOOD NUMBER: Cox & Kings had a famous brand, reported profits and an international footprint, and looked like a cheap way to own Indian outbound travel. WHY IT LIED: travel operators collect money from customers before paying hotels and airlines, so the model should run on negative working capital and little debt. Cox & Kings instead carried heavy and rising debt and large receivables and advances, with CFO persistently weak relative to profit. A lender-appointed PwC audit later found ~Rs 4,367 cr siphoned and books manipulated from Apr 2014 to Jun 2019; foreign subsidiaries allegedly forged audit reports and bank statements that Indian auditors consolidated. CP default 26 Jun 2019; stock to ~Rs 2-3 from Rs 250-400. TEST: write down the working-capital sign the business model implies (DMart, Bharti, airlines, travel = negative) and compare with the balance sheet; a mismatch means either a bad business or wrong accounts. Check which audit firm signs each material subsidiary. LESSON: the simplest forensic test is coherence between business model and balance sheet; brand age is not evidence.

body:
`insight:flag-negative-fcf-context` · verified

RULE: negative FCF is benign when CFO is positive and the capex earns high returns on proven demand (DMart's owned stores, Bharti's network, APL Apollo's DFT lines), when it funds a durable asset that scales (Netflix content 2018-19: FCF -$3.0 bn and -$3.27 bn, positive from 2020), or when negative CFO reflects a lender's loan growth (Bajaj Finance: negative every year FY15-26 while ROE stayed ~20%). Low CFO/PAT is benign when the working capital is liquid and the business's own (Titan: CFO/PAT 0.62 over FY15-26 because of gold inventory in its stores, funded by gold loans, debtor days 4-8) or when the debtor is sovereign and the delay is budgetary (HAL FY17-19). IT IS SUSPECT WHEN: (1) CFO is weak while receivables or 'loans and advances' grow faster than sales (PC Jeweller exports, Ricoh unbilled revenue, Cox & Kings); (2) the working-capital sign contradicts the business model (a travel company or retailer should be negative); (3) 'capex' goes to related parties or CWIP ages without commissioning; (4) CFO is propped by factoring or customer funds (GE, Wirecard). WARNING: the CFO/PAT test can pass in a trap (Vakrangee FY17-18 CFO > PAT), so it is necessary, not sufficient. TEST: split the cash gap into capex (growth vs maintenance), inventory, receivables (by counterparty), and loans; name the asset created; check incremental ROCE on capex completed 2-3 years ago.

- **History:** DCs were added in 2019–22 at ~900–1,200 stores, and expanded in 2024. No new DC is announced ("evaluate opportunities"). **Open item:** management's stated network capacity in stores. The next DC (~$60–90M) is the lumpy capex the store model omits.
